card.title: Nintendo Switch Blue screen of death Repair

source.title: Nintendo Switch Blue screen of death Repair

claims.statement: Switch blue screen is usually cracked solder balls or broken traces under the CPU or RAM from the thin board bending.
Press on the bowed IC while powering/charging (both RAM chips if needed); a Nintendo logo identifies the chip. Brief low heat (150–200 °C, 10–20 s) on each IC can also reveal it.

A reflow (375–450 °C, no nozzle, until the IC nudges and springs back) is a quick but often temporary fix; a reball (magnetic stencil recommended for the CPU) is the lasting fix; occasionally eMMC is the cause.
Replace thermal paste between CPU and shield and between shield and heatsink on reassembly.

procedure: Look for board bowing over CPU/RAM.
Press on each chip while powering to find the culprit.
Reflow, or remove, rebuild ripped pads and reball the chip.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Heat while the board is in the frame can damage the plastic and LCD.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
